headline: Operational area extended to waters south of Oman, +P-8A patrol aircraft, EOD team and unmanned mine-countermeasure systems, +75
dek: Seoul will submit a revised Cheonghae deployment mandate (Cabinet endorsement next week, then National Assembly consent) extending the unit's area from the Gulf of Aden northeast to open waters south of Oman in the Arabian Sea, roughly doubling its operational radius to about 1,930 km; adds a P-8A…
sources: Yonhap News Agency (Kim Seung-yeon), citing South Korean officials / Defence Ministry plan
fault_line: Is Seoul's 'closer to Hormuz, but not in it' expansion prudent protection of Korean shipping, or a first step into the US-Iran war by stealth?

sections.what_happened: Seoul will submit a revised Cheonghae deployment mandate (Cabinet endorsement next week, then National Assembly consent) extending the unit's area from the Gulf of Aden northeast to open waters south of Oman in the Arabian Sea, roughly doubling its operational radius to about 1,930 km; adds a P-8A maritime patrol aircraft, an EOD team and unmanned mine-countermeasure equipment to the 4,400-ton destroyer Chungmugong Yi Sun-sin, raising personnel from 320 to 395. Operations stay in open waters south of Oman; the P-8A is prohibited from targeting/monitoring Iranian territory, territorial waters or the interior of the Strait of Hormuz; entering Hormuz itself with non-combat assets would need separate parliamentary approval. The EOD/mine systems are framed as preparation for possible post-war international mine-clearing in Hormuz. Current mandate expires Dec 31.
sections.what_verified: Yonhap wire report carried/relayed by Korea Herald, AJ liveblog and Seoul Economic Daily; the underlying announcement is a single government plan, so distinct-family count stays at 1 declared family (Yonhap T2). Seoul Economic Daily and Korea Herald items in this check carry the Yonhap report and have no separate declared tier counted here.
sections.what_disputed: Opposition (Rebuilding Korea Party floor leader Kim Joon-hyung, Nov 4, Korea Herald) calls the expansion an effective troop deployment that could draw Seoul into the US-Iran conflict; the government counters with four principles (no war involvement/intervention, protection of ROK nationals/ships, open-seas-south-of-Oman limit, independent command). The plan is NOT yet approved: Cabinet + Assembly consent still pending, so no deployment has happened.
sections.why_matters: Monitor only: a PROPOSAL in the proven shipping/Hormuz lane with hard numbers (1,930 km, 320→395, P-8A), but nothing has deployed and the unit explicitly stops short of Hormuz. It becomes a Short only on Cabinet endorsement / Assembly vote, or if the mandate's Hormuz-entry clause is triggered. PortWatch context (STALE): IMF PortWatch counted 4 transits through Hormuz on 2026-10-18, 7-day average 3.7 vs a 2025 baseline of 85.5/day — snapshot fetched Oct 26, stale flag true, now 18 days old; cite only with that date and staleness, never as a live count.
sections.context: Background: IN-WINDOW (Yonhap Nov 5, 09:30 KST = 04:30 ; AJ liveblog 01:15 GMT = 05:15 , relaying Yonhap) — South Korea to expand Cheonghae anti-piracy unit toward Hormuz: operational area extended to waters south of Oman, +P-8A patrol aircraft, EOD team and unmanned mine-countermeasure systems, +75 personnel to 395
